what: Cost, lead-time and time numbers for the robot-built desktop LPBF video (issue #260, PR #266, round 7)
how_to_show: Tour the categories in the order of 'categories'. For each, show hud.new (at spec, all new) against hud.used (the used picks where a sensible listing exists, new elsewhere) and the running totals hud.run_new / hud.run_used; hud.range_new / hud.range_used are the BOM's full low-high ranges. Call out the category's 'items' in order with their hud.new, hud.used, hud.lead_new and hud.lead_used. 'offtable' and 'services' are not on the table: show them as text rows at the end of the tour.

definitions.used: 'Used majors': the 13 used picks of cost/used-options.csv re-based on today's bom.csv (USED_REBASE) plus a refurbished UPS for D2; for each component and end, the cheaper of new and used

definitions.spec_new: cost_scenarios.py's at-spec rule: the CW optics chain (L1, L3, L5, L6, C1) at its BOM high end, the cheapest listed option on every other line (L2 = 0: the quoted IPG is air-cooled)

machining.method:
There is no credible published rule for CAM hours (the search for one found none), so CAM time is a stated estimate:
  CAM = 0.5 h + 0.6 h per setup + 0.015 h per hole (+ 1 h for a lathe-and-mill part, + 8 h for the old block's deep pocket:
        long-tool strategies, rest machining of the R5 corners and coves, holder checks at 120 mm).
Setups: the count from setup_plan.json (3-axis, or with a 4th axis where it swings inside an HRT210 and saves a setup), at
  0.75 h each for parts that fit a vise and 1.25 h for parts over 300 mm (fixture plate, toe clamps, probing); the first rotary
  setup 1.5 h. Modern Machine Shop's survey median is 68-90 min per setup (last good part to first good part).
Run: dfm.py's conservative model (16 cm3/min roughing in 6061, 3 in 316L; 40 / 10 cm2/min finishing; per-hole times) for every
  part, and for the chamber also setup_plan.py's vendor-feed model (Helical / Haas data, 60 % efficiency).
Deburr and inspect: 0.25 h a part, 1 h for a part with a sealing face.
Programmed run (frame and floor plate only, since 2026-11-25): the cutting time of freecad_cam.py's posted G-code for every
  setup (frame B, A and setup C's four A indexes; floor A and B), as CAMotics counts it with the VF-4's 25.4 m/min rapids
  (camotics_sim.py; else freecad_cam.py's recount), plus 4.2 s per tool change (VF-4 tool to tool) and 3 s per A index
  (ASSUMED: unclamp, index, clamp). The taps, STI taps, reamers, spot drills and SAE port tools are not programmed, so this
  is a floor on the run time, not a replacement for the two estimates.
The 'before' column is the 37-part review in machining.md (dfm.json at 2026-11-20 14:00-22:00 UTC, the block chamber body).

chamber.note: frame + floor plate; setups include 0.5 h on the waterjet; vendor run time adds 45 min of waterjet; the programmed run time is the posted G-code's (taps, reamers and port tools not programmed), without the waterjet

Robot time = 30 s per placement + the insertion path from sequence.json at 10 mm/s, 20 s + 15 s a screw, 90 s an O-ring or cord, 30 s a flip, 60 s a two-arm carry, 15 s a tool change; MiR trips to the long table are counted per chapter (4 parts a trip, 140 s a round trip). Person minutes per step are listed in build_hud.py (PERSON_MIN), 1 min per screw the arm couldn't drive and 5 min per failed placement.
